title: Introduction to Information Technology
description: This is an introductory personal computer applications course. It includes the operating system (MS Windows), word processing (MS Word), spreadsheets (MS Excel), and presentation manager (MS PowerPoint), database applications (MS Access)

title: Introduction to Generative AI
description: This course provides an introduction to essential software applications, including the operating system (MS Windows), word processing (MS Word), spreadsheets (MS Excel), and presentation management (MS PowerPoint). It also explores Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its practical applications across various industries. Designed for students without prior IT experience, the course emphasizes hands-on learning to develop practical skills. Students will gain an understanding of core concepts and learn to effectively use Generative AI tools. Key topics include crafting effective prompts, recognizing ethical considerations, and leveraging AI for creative problem-solving

title: English I
description: The course is designed for college students to benefit from an intensive skill-building curriculum that targets the main English skills. The focus of the course will be on reading and writing skill practice, grammar and structure application, and integration across the disciplines at the college-level. Students will be expected to successfully demonstrate and apply appropriate college-level reading and writing skills to a variety of assignments and assessments. Competences in contextualized reading and writing skills will be developed. Active reading and writing strategies will be learned through practice and application. title: English II
description: This is a writing course that helps students become competent writers by engaging them in the writing process and by encouraging them to explore and organize their ideas in writing well-organized and developed paragraphs and essays. Students also study grammar, basic sentence structure and mechanics. Written and communication Skills will be developed and improved to prepare students for future careers

title: Logic and Critical Thinking
description: Critical Thinking is a course designed to help students develop their skills in reasoning, analysis, and the use of logical arguments. This course introduces students to the standards of critical thinking, nature of arguments, deductive and inductive reasoning, fallacious reasoning, role of language, critical analysis, and evaluation. The students are also introduced to the basic skills of good reasoning needed for the intelligent and responsible conduct of life. The course also includes the application of concepts in familiar areas and current issues, to help students develop practical and useful logical and critical thinking skills to understand and appreciate viewpoints which are different from their own

title: Psychology
description: This course is capstone course that attempts to addresses the major theories, principles, and methodologies of psychology with special emphasis on their relations to human behavior. The biological foundations of behavior, sensory processes, learning, perception, memory, emotion, motivation, personality, and the social basis of behavior are examined

title: Fundamentals of Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: This course seeks to prepare students how to apply core concepts regarding design thinking process, innovation, entrepreneurship and sustainability to organizations in the UAE. Students will learn how to connect entrepreneurship to the UAE community and economy and how as entrepreneurs can utilize design thinking and innovation to establish their start-up enterprises Design thinking, Entrepreneurship, and Growth and Leadership are three modules that will be covered throughout course delivery, study questions, videos, and projects

title: Ethics
description: This course exposes students to core concepts, ideals and practical issues regarding professional ethics and moral behaviors. The history and development, ethical guidelines/principles and contemporary theories of the subject- matter will be the focus of the introductory chapter. Furthermore, discussions will concentrate on the relevance of Professional Ethics to modern workplaces and environments. Morality and liability, employees and moral choices, employers, and moral choices, are themes which will be covered throughout course delivery, exams and case studies

title: Mathematics and Statistics
description: This course introduces some mathematical concepts needed for success and facing this century life. It covers different topics like; basic concepts of mathematics, such as ratios and proportions, general algebra, linear equations, and linear and exponential functions by graphing them. Additionally, it covers the basic concepts of statistics and how to analyze statistical results

title: Introduction to Management
description: This course aims to introduce students with knowledge of the principles, functions and techniques of management to gain a solid background in business organization and management. Essential topics examined in this course include management functions, decision-making, motivation, communication. Special attention is paid to the cultural and regional context of business organizations. This course expected to serve as a foundation for other courses in business

title: Accounting Principles I
description: This course is an introduction to financial accounting methods such as recording and book- keeping in the journal, ledger, and trial balance in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). This course is designed to help students apply the appropriate accounting treatment for both adjusting and closing operations. It also helps students in recording business transactions of merchandising companies, calculating cost of inventories, and illustrating internal control and bank reconciliation statement

title: Introduction to Marketing
description: This course introduces the students to basic marketing concepts and terminology and integrates learning material with real world examples. Areas covered include: the marketing concept, marketing mix, the marketing environment, marketing information and research, consumer behavior, pricing strategies and market segmentation

title: Accounting Principles II
description: This course introduces advanced accounting concepts to students, including different forms of ownership, cash flows statemen, financial analysis, accounting for manufacturing operations. The purpose of this course is to provide the students with the basis of accounting skills required in Business Administration to be used in the business environment for decision making

title: Introduction to Human Resource Management
description: This course introduces various areas of human resource management including its strategic role, job analysis, training and development, HR planning and recruitment, employee selection, training and developing employees, performance management, strategic pay plans, employee relations, and employee safety & health in the workplace

title: Microeconomics
description: This course is an introductory course in economic theory and applications. It will familiarize the students with the basic principles of microeconomics. Topics that will be covered include behavior of households and firms, consumption possibilities & preferences, production functions and market structures

title: Organizational Behavior
description: This course examines the complex relationships among individuals, groups, organizations, and society. It emphasizes a dynamic systems approach to understanding and facilitating work relationships through the study of the interaction of individual needs, abilities, and traits with organizational goals and structures. Some of the contemporary organizational issues included in this course are individual and group dynamics, motivation and performance, leadership, power, organizational culture, organizational change, and development

title: Management Information Systems
description: This course is designed to introduce the Management Information systems concepts within the context of the business environment. It provides comprehensive and integrative coverage of essential new information technologies and their impact on business models and managerial decision-making. The course provides an integrated framework by showing how information systems are composed of management, organization, and technology elements

title: Business Statistics
description: This course will introduce the learner to some techniques in descriptive and inferential statistics. Topics included are data presentation using different tools, central measures, dispersion measures, introduction to probability, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, and computer applications

title: Macroeconomics
description: This course provides an understanding of the role and methodology of economics, components of the economy, roles of government and central bank in the economy through fiscal policy, monetary policy, and system. This course also covers macroeconomic indicators (GDP, Inflation, and Unemployment), economic growth and the business cycle

title: Introduction to Financial Management
description: This course is prepared to equip students with the fundamentals of financial management. It includes an overview of financial management, analysis of financial Statement, time value of money, risk and return, working capital management, financial statement analysis, sources of finance, and capital budgeting

title: Quantitative Business Analysis
description: This course provides a comprehensive survey of the main quantitative business techniques used in business analysis and decision making, in particular the application of mathematical and statistical models in the analysis of problems related to economic and administrative sciences. The main topic includes decision making analysis under uncertainty, regression analysis and hypothesis testing, forecasting techniques, linear programming models and network analysis

title: Research Methods
description: The course is designed to introduce students to qualitative and quantitative research methods, as well as commonly used statistical procedures in data analysis. Topics covered include the role of business research, scientific inquiry, the research process, proposal development, research design, hypothesis testing, primary and secondary data collection, statistical data analysis and presentation of research reports. The ethical issues of research design and data interpretation will also be discussed

title: Operations Management
description: This course provides a foundation in fundamental concepts, techniques and applications of contemporary production and operations management to serve as tools for improving quality, productivity and international competitiveness. It covers a selection of quantitative tools and techniques to aid in decision making and operations management setting. Topics such as forecasting, product and service development, capacity planning, process selection, facility planning, quality management and inventory management will be introduced. The concepts for designing, planning and improving manufacturing and service organizations will also be examined

title: Strategic Management
description: This course is capstone course that attempts to addresses the main areas of strategic management process and assessment of how company’s strategy interacts with and guides within its external and internal environments. The focus of the course is on business unit and corporate-level strategy, strategy formulating, strategy implementation, and covering the overall strategic management process. Also, it examines how organizations can sustain competitive advantage and how corporate strategies can be implemented successfully. The course covers strategic implementation as its relation to strategic leadership, organizational structure, and culture. Case analyses and text material are employed to integrate student’s knowledge and improve strategic thinking skills

title: International Business Management
description: This course is capstone course that attempts to addresses the main areas of strategic management process and assessment of how company’s strategy interacts with and guides within its external and internal environments. The focus of the course is on business unit and corporate-level strategy, strategy formulating, strategy implementation, and covering the overall strategic management process. The course covers strategic implementation as its relation to strategic leadership, organizational structure, and culture. title: Introduction to Computer Programming
description: Introduction to Computer Programming (ICP) is an introductory course designed to provide students with fundamental knowledge and skills in computer programming. The course covers key programming concepts, including problem-solving techniques, algorithm development, pseudocode, flowcharts, programming syntax, variables, data types, control structures, loops, arrays and functions. Students will build practical skills and explore how programming can support real-world and sustainability-focused solutions

title: Object Oriented Programming
description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of Object- Oriented Programming (OOP) using the Java programming language. It covers essential OOP principles such as classes, objects, encapsulation, method overloading and overriding, static methods, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, and interfaces. Students will also explore input/output (I/O) operations using Java streams and learn how to connect and interact with relational databases using JDBC. In addition, the course teaches good practices in Graphical User Interface (GUI) development and emphasizes building real-world applications using a modular, object-oriented approach. Students are encouraged to develop solutions that contribute to sustainability and responsible digital innovation

title: Introduction to Web Development
description: This course is an introduction to Web Development using HTML language. It covers the following elements: Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), Cascading Style Sheets for creating web- formed Web pages that are compliant with current Web standards and how to publish students’ Web sites. In addition, this course covers the application of JavaScript and DHTML as client-side programming. Students will learn the best practices for sustainable web design, such as optimizing images and scripts, minimizing resource usage, and ensuring accessibility and usability

title: E-Business
description: this course develops the student’s understanding of basic principles of e-business and ecommerce management, functions, technologies, and goals. The course covers e-business models, strategies, and applications with the explanation of most computer jargon and terminology relevant to e-commerce

title: Database Management Systems
description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of database systems, including database architecture, data models, and system components. It emphasizes the design of efficient relational databases using ER diagrams and their conversion into optimized schemas. Students will learn various normalization techniques to ensure data integrity, minimize redundancy, and support sustainable data storage. The course also provides a solid foundation in relational algebra and hands-on experience in SQL programming

title: Business Intelligence
description: This course illustrates the applicability of Business Intelligence (BI) in the development of successful business models. It investigates the role of data mining for BI in an organization. Students will first learn appropriate tools and techniques for data pre-processing and data exploration. Then, they will explore and apply some supervised and unsupervised data mining techniques to create valuable strategies and make wiser business decisions

title: Object Oriented Systems Analysis and Design
description: This course introduces the principles and design techniques of object-oriented development approaches. It focuses on the process of developing information systems using object-oriented system analysis and design techniques based on the Unified Modeling Language (UML). Students will learn key concepts and methods used in the object-oriented system development process, including problem identification, application of object- oriented concepts and tools in problem solving, data gathering, modeling, analysis, project management, and design. The course also covers UML diagrams, validation techniques to assess model quality, and methods to ensure system requirements are met. Additionally, sustainable application design principles are emphasized to create reliable, long-term solutions

title: Data Communications and Networking
description: In this course students are going to be introduced to the basic computer network concepts and elements. Students will be taught the characteristics of network models, topologies, network devices, data transmission, and communication protocols going through more detail about IP addressing. Students will be introduced to network simulation tools to apply their theoretical knowledge to practical aspects. This course will also explore the concept of basic network data security, privacy, and sustainable networks

title: Graduation Project
description: This course offers students a unique opportunity to apply their learning about business technology and the entire software development lifecycle, from business needs to deployment. It amplifies classroom instruction about IT project planning and implementation. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. Students may work individually or in teams and must deliver a complete product (Application, website, planning designs, etc.) at the end of the course

title: Information Security
description: This course provides a foundational understanding of information and network security principles. It introduces key security concepts, terminology, and models essential for recognizing and addressing modern security challenges. Further, it explores various types of threats, including network attacks, computer-based attacks, and social engineering techniques. The course covers basic cryptographic methods, server vulnerabilities, and both wired and wireless network security infrastructure. Emphasis is placed on authentication mechanisms, vulnerability assessments, and the design and implementation of sustainable security solutions for stand-alone and networked systems

title: Advanced Web Development
description: This course provides practical knowledge for designing and developing web-based applications using modern web development techniques. It focuses on HTML, CSS, and dynamic web content through interactive web technologies. Students will learn how to build dynamic web applications that integrate with databases. Throughout the course, students will work with advanced web techniques and technologies to develop a dynamic web application, including client-side tools, server-side technologies, and database connectivity. The course also introduces the concept of sustainable web design, emphasizing efficient coding practices and environmental considerations in web development

title: Advanced Database Management Systems
description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of sustainable database design and application development. It covers the implementation of both basic and advanced SQL queries optimized for efficiency and performance. The course emphasizes the development of database applications using PL/SQL and the creation of essential database objects, including views, triggers, procedures, functions, and packages. Key database management system (DBMS) concepts such as transaction processing, concurrency control, and recovery are explored to ensure data integrity, consistency, and reliability. Additionally, the design and development of user-friendly graphical interfaces using forms and reports are covered

title: Internship
description: The course requires students to complete a set number of hours in a private or public organization. Students may choose to undertake their internship in any area of business administration. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of Liwa University. Elective Courses

title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
description: This course provides an overview of critical issues faced in small business and entrepreneurship. This includes an overview of how strategic planning, operations, human resources and financial management issues are related to small business and entrepreneurs. This course also provides the student with a broad understanding of the basic issues in modern operations management in both manufacturing and service organizations. It focuses on the development of a strategic business plan and competitive business model for a small business or entrepreneurial venture. Special emphasis is placed on adapting business skills to the realistic needs of a small business owner and entrepreneur

title: Financial Institutions and Markets
description: This course provides the learner with an overview on the operation of the financial system within the framework of modern economic and finance theory. It focuses on financial institutions and their role in financial intermediation, financial instruments, and pricing in primary and secondary, stock markets. It also focuses on the share price analysis in global markets and forward and future markets in financial risk management

title: Consumer Behavior
description: This course is an introduction to the world of consumer behavior. The discipline derives from several social sciences including psychology, sociology, and marketing to explain the behavior of the customer in the marketplace. In this course, the student will understand how personality, perceptions, learning, and attitudes affect consumption behavior. Additionally, to explore how consumption changes during one’s life cycle, and how powerful cultural and subcultural influences are on consumers

title: Change Management
description: This course introduces an overview of change situations, and the issues and methods associated with the management of change. The topics covered include identifying the need for change, planning and communicating change, strategies for implementing change, and overcoming resistance to change. Students will also examine the role of leadership and the competencies and skills required of individuals who initiate, manage, and are affected by change. In addition, the students will be given an overview of the evolution of computers and the associated technologies together with a presentation of future technological trends

In addition, this course discusses database problems and potential solutions and how to improve database performance, productivity, and portability through different integration patterns with DBMSs and programming languages in accordance with software application requirements

title: Discrete Mathematics
description: This course enables students to strengthen and increase their understanding of discrete mathematics with special emphasis on computer science applications. title: Information Security Management
description: This course focuses on the managerial aspects of information security and assurance. Topics covered include access control models, information security governance, and information security program assessment and metrics. Coverage on the foundational and technical components of information security is included in reinforcing key concepts. The course includes up- to-date information on changes in the field, such as national and international laws and international standards like the ISO 27000 series, Risk Management, Security Mechanisms, and Blockchain concepts and applications. Sustainable security practices are emphasized to ensure long-term protection, efficiency, and responsible resource management

title: Linear Algebra
description: This course is an introduction to Linear Algebra and some of its applications. The aim is to teach the fundamentals of linear algebra in a way that illustrates their relevance to business mathematics applications. An Introduction to Matrices and Systems of Linear Equations are given with other topics such as Determinants, Linear Transformations, Eigenvectors and Eigen values. Techniques and application of business mathematics of linear algebra for finance sciences, management, and economics

title: Internship
description: This is a supervised course requiring a minimum of 480 hours of structured, industry-based training in Information Technology or related fields. The internship provides students with the opportunity to apply technical skills and academic knowledge to solve real-world IT problems while gaining exposure to current tools, technologies, and practices used in industry, with a focus on sustainability and responsible innovation. Through this experience, students enhance their professional competencies, including teamwork, communication, and time management, and develop an understanding of ethical, social, and environmental considerations in professional IT contexts. Student performance is continuously monitored by an assigned faculty supervisor in collaboration with the workplace supervisor through regular evaluations and progress reviews

title: User Interface Design
description: This course covers user interface design within the software development process, integrating cognitive theories relevant to effective interaction. It includes usability requirements specification and evaluation, emphasizing a multi-disciplinary approach. Students learn to assess user needs and capabilities and how this influence UI development through iterative design phases such as data gathering, analysis, prototyping, construction, and evaluation. The course introduces green computing principles and eco-friendly design practices. Students will use industry-standard tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, Axure RP, and Sketch for wireframing and prototyping; Miro for collaborative brainstorming and user journey mapping; and Usability Hub or Hotjar for usability testing and feedback gathering

title: Calculus I
description: Calculus is an exciting subject, justly considered to be one of the greatest achievements of the human intellect. Today calculus is used not just in the physical sciences, but also in engineering, business, economics, life sciences, and social sciences—any discipline that seeks to understand dynamic phenomena. Part of the aim of this course is to train the student to think logically. Learn to write the solutions of the exercises in a connected, step- by-step fashion with explanatory sentences—not just a string of disconnected equations or formulas. This course is intended to introduce derivatives, one of the two key concepts of calculus. The second is integral. Both key concepts depend on the notion of limit

title: Mobile Applications Development
description: This course provides comprehensive knowledge related to designing, developing, and deploying mobile applications and websites, aligning with industry practices. It covers design principles, tools, techniques, and methods for mobile application development, including user interface design, data management, security, privacy, and ethics. Students will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard frameworks, testing tools, and deployment methods, preparing them to create secure, scalable, and sustainable mobile applications for diverse industry sectors

title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
description: This course introduces undergraduate students to the fundamental concepts and techniques in Artificial Intelligence (AI). Students will explore how intelligent systems can be designed to solve problems using methods such as search algorithms, rule-based reasoning, and basic machine learning. The course covers key areas including knowledge representation, natural language processing, and AI applications in areas such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and sustainability. Emphasis is placed on how AI technologies can contribute to addressing global challenges such as energy efficiency, climate change, and smart resource management

title: Senior Graduation Project I
description: This course provides students with the opportunity to explore a chosen area of interest, conduct in-depth research, and demonstrate independent learning, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Students will apply research methodologies and concepts acquired in earlier coursework to develop a comprehensive project proposal. The process involves selecting a topic, gathering and analyzing relevant information, formulating a clear problem statement, conducting a literature review, and proposing feasible and innovative solutions. Students are expected to apply appropriate methodologies to analyze the problem and develop an initial system design aligned with sustainability principles. Particular emphasis is placed on incorporating environmental, economic, and social dimensions of sustainability into the project’s design and planning. By the end of the course, students will present a preliminary system design and submit a detailed project report that highlights the project’s potential contribution to sustainable development goals (SDGs)

title: Senior Graduation Project II
description: This supervised course is the continuation of Senior Graduation Project I (CIT484), in which students are expected to fully implement their proposed solution. Building on the design phase and documentation developed in SGP1, students will complete the remaining phases of the project, detailed design, system implementation, testing, validation, and final documentation. Throughout the course, students will apply project management practices, adhere to software engineering methodologies, and receive weekly guidance from their academic supervisor. The course emphasizes sustainable development by encouraging the integration of environmentally and socially responsible practices, such as energy efficiency, ethical data usage, and alignment with national and global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The course fosters teamwork, independent problem-solving, ethical responsibility, and effective communication, equipping students with practical and professional skills essential for real-world IT project execution. Elective Courses

title: Internet of Things
description: This course introduces the architecture, protocols, and real- world applications of the Internet of Things (IoT). Students will explore core concepts such as connectivity, interoperability, discoverability, security/privacy, and sustainability in IoT ecosystems. Emphasis is placed on IoT applications in smart cities, industry, and environmental monitoring. The student will be presented to some tools used for building IoT setup, such as TinkerCAD, Arduino simulators, Linux OS, and Python programming environments

title: Cloud and Edge Computing
description: This course covers important concepts, architectures, and service models in an in-depth examination of cloud and edge computing. Theoretical lectures, practical exercises, and case studies give students a thorough understanding of the networking, virtualization, and distributed computing technologies that support these paradigms. Working with top cloud platforms and edge computing frameworks to deploy, maintain, and optimize apps is what practical workshops entail. Additionally, the course explores how cloud and edge computing contribute to sustainability by enabling energy-efficient resource management, reducing data transmission overhead, and supporting green IT initiatives. The course also looks at actual use cases from a variety of industries to show how edge and cloud computing technologies are enabling creative solutions and revolutionizing corporate processes

title: Natural Language Processing
description: This course explores the theory and practical aspects of processing human language using computational methods. Topics include text preprocessing, language modeling, part-of- speech tagging, syntactic parsing, semantic analysis, and pragmatic analysis. It also covers applications of NLP techniques such as Named Entity Recognition, Question and Answering Systems, Sentiment Analysis, Topic Modeling, and Sentiment Analysis. Students will gain hands-on experience with NLP tools and libraries. The course also explores how NLP can contribute to sustainability by supporting environmental text analysis and informed decision-making

title: Data Mining
description: This course introduces the principles of data mining to the students. The students will learn preprocessing of data (data cleaning, data reduction etc.) before applying data mining techniques. Some of the data mining techniques covered in this course are classification, association analysis, and clustering. Students will learn about the social and ethical aspects of data mining. Additionally, the course explores how data mining can support sustainability goals, such as optimizing resource consumption and supporting environmental data analysis. General Track Courses

title: Software Development Process
description: This course presents an introduction to the models, processes, and techniques used in developing software systems. It covers the entire life cycle of software systems, from project proposal and requirements analysis through design, development, testing, release, and maintenance. Students are introduced to industry-standard techniques such as fact-finding, software modeling, verification and validation, and system documentation. In alignment with the UAE's sustainability vision and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, this course incorporates eco-conscious software engineering principles. Students are exposed to the Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) Tool from the Green Software Foundation, enabling them to evaluate and reduce the environmental impact of their software designs

title: Network Administration
description: This course introduces concepts and technologies behind domain-based enterprise networks. The course covers installation, configuration and administration of enterprise network operating systems and protocols, and services such as active directory, group policies, data storage, backup and disaster recovery to the level required to effectively administer a secured domain-based enterprise networks for both traditional networks and green networks

title: Distributed Information Management
description: This course provides a comprehensive examination of distributed information systems, which serve as the backbone of modern global organizations. It addresses the fundamental principles of distributed architecture, processes, communication protocols, consistency models, and fault tolerance mechanisms. Students will analyze components of distributed IT infrastructure, including operating systems, naming conventions, and communication frameworks. Particular emphasis is placed on the integration of sustainability principles, focusing on energy- efficient design, environmentally responsible computing practices, and the selection of sustainable cloud services. The course aims to equip students with both the theoretical foundation and practical insights required to design and manage distributed systems that are robust, scalable, and sustainable

title: Advanced Database Design
description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of advanced database design, with a particular emphasis on data warehouse architecture and implementation using industry-relevant tools. Students will engage in conceptual, logical, and physical design stages while examining key topics such as big data management, database administration, and integration with web services. Practical skills will be developed through hands-on use of platforms such as MySQL, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server for relational databases, and Power BI for business intelligence and dashboard creation. The course also introduces NoSQL systems (e.g., MongoDB) and cloud-based environments (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure) to emphasize sustainable data storage and processing. Sustainable database design principles, including energy efficiency, optimized queries, and responsible cloud resource use are woven throughout the course to prepare students for building scalable, high-performance, and environmentally responsible data systems
